decisions.reason: The reference electrometer sits at the core of the firm's dosimetry expertise and has been featured on the home page for two years, so it is likely meeting aspirations and gives no reason for search.

The oncology risk management software extends the firm's software integration strategy and has kept its own page since 2023, and an expanding firm has the slack to keep carrying it while results build up.
The CT phantom builds on the firm's established imaging QA line, and in a growing industry with an expanding firm there is no performance shortfall that would prompt dropping it.
This mammography phantom is distant from the core offer and its results are uncertain, but it is only one year old and organisational slack lets the firm tolerate the risk while it learns.
The full field mammography phantom overlaps with Product D in a distant segment, which makes it the most likely candidate for consolidation, yet early-stage slack favours keeping it for now.
The broad line of medical imaging QA instruments fits the firm's strategic direction and established capabilities, so it is likely to be kept.
